english: The actual picture was obviously burnt away in the blast.
Sad to see it ruined like this.
Drummer does strike me as the type of guy to hang a giant picture of himself.
Self-portrait sounds about right. These bird-folk only care about themselves.
I bet it was a painting of a door.
He scoffs. "Drummer's a copycat. He just copies humans."
I'm extremely humble. Clerics have to be. It's in the rules.
I have a medium <u>ego</u>. Perfectly average.
He elbows you from the side.
He holds out his hands, measuring the size of a tea pot.
It's good to be <u>ego</u>tistical. Healthy, even.
The goblin does not meet your gaze.
I am a Wizard, after all.
I don't know him personally or anything, but that bird's flying solo.
They don't have to be real.
It could be an imaginary wife and kids.
He's contemplating your words. Then dismisses them.
A door. Like, to trick people.
They'd walk into the wall. They'd go 'Hey, I can't grab the handle!'
Maybe we should keep looking for actual clues.
Are you saying this burned painting is not a clue?
Fuck it. Sure. It's a clue.
He lets out a big sigh.
That's a strange thing to think. Paintings are great opportunities to show off your visual aesthetic.
Yes. It is a tragedy. All art is sacred.
You have no way of knowing if it was even beautiful.
It could have been some horrific abomination of a painting.
There is beauty in all art.
Such anti-canonical thought is exactly why art has lost its meaning.
This frame must have been beautiful, before it burned.
It was most likely just an LR. Who pays for actual art these days?
Iron. Melted to hell, but still somewhat intact.
Not as affected by the fire as some pipes you saw in the central tea shop chamber.
Strange. You feel a slight breeze.
(Look for the source of the breeze.)
The wall. The wall is not a wall.
No signs beyond that left by the flames.
